summary: Independent review reproduced the original accumulated quadratic host-CPU rollback-history work on the prepared base and verified that the exact candidate replaces full-history slice/rebind with guarded in-place deletion. On the actual installed xgrammar matcher, the candidate preserved rollback boundaries and list identity, fixed rollback(0) history desynchronization, and changed 8x-size accumulated timing growth from 21.33x to 7.88x (approximately linear in the number of operations).

tests.what_was_measured: Actual XGrammarGrammar plus installed xgrammar.GrammarMatcher, using repeated speculative accept/rollback(1) followed by one committed accept so history accumulates. Median seconds for N=2000/4000/8000/16000 were 0.003653/0.009004/0.025060/0.077904; doubling ratios 2.465/2.783/3.109 and 8x-size ratio 21.328 reproduced superlinear accumulated work. Boundary assertions also reproduced rollback(0) debug-history desynchronization and list rebinding.
Candidate regression on the real matcher: rollback(0), partial/full history truncation, content, and in-place list identity; 2 tests passed.

Unchanged independent actual-backend workload. All empty/zero/partial/full boundaries and identity checks passed. Median seconds were 0.002444/0.004853/0.009613/0.019249; doubling ratios 1.986/1.981/2.002 and 8x-size ratio 7.877, consistent with linear total work.
Candidate-provided actual-backend controlled CPU benchmark; medians 0.002386/0.004748/0.009490/0.019009 seconds with doubling ratios 1.990/1.999/2.003.

gpu_execution.evidence: No GPU kernels or model generation were run. The assigned device was visible as one AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015. The reviewed contract concerns Python host-CPU list-copy complexity, so timings are explicitly CPU timings, not GPU performance claims.

The actual native xgrammar package loaded from /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/xgrammar, while the reviewed backend loaded from /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/constrained/xgrammar_backend.py.
remaining_limitations: No live speculative-decoding server or model generation was run; verification isolates the exact actual-backend accept/rollback/commit pattern responsible for the reported host work.
No GPU performance conclusion is made.
The installed xgrammar emits a deprecation warning that max_rollback_tokens is now always unlimited, although the SGLang constant is 200; this does not affect the verified Python history-copy fix.

Negative rollback counts are accepted unusually by the installed matcher, but are outside SGLang's rollback caller contract and the candidate preserves the base implementation's effective Python-list behavior for that invalid input.
